messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed inconsistent client-side behavior when we route to fallback models. Some SDKs surface 429, others show 503. This is confusing for customers. Can we align on an error taxonomy + console UX for degraded routes?
laura: +1. We need a clear distinction between quota/backpressure vs degraded-quality fallbacks. Customers shouldn't assume retry on quality fallback.
ben: Quick context: runtime currently returns 429 for 'rate limit' and 503 for 'no-capacity / fallback path applied' in some handlers. Different teams mapped those differently in SDKs.
carla: From runtime side, fallback to smaller model is treated as a successful response with a warning, but when we drop requests to burst queue we return 503. The ambiguity is from partial failures in routing layer.
dmitri: Telemetry concern: we need distinct tags so ops can filter degradations vs hard failures. Propose: tag = {route_outcome: normal|degraded|failed}, and a separate client_error_kind header for SDKs.
emily: For console we should show a single consolidated badge but let users click into the event type. Suggested badge states: green/healthy, yellow/degraded (fallbacks/routed-to-slower), red-failed (errors).
alex: Agree on labels. Also need a client-facing mapping doc: when should SDKs retry? only on transient failed==true. For degraded responses we should NOT advise retry.
laura: What about HTTP status choices? Options: 1) Keep 200 + body-level warning for degraded model (no retry) 2) Use 2xx with header X-Redwood-Route: degraded 3) Use 503 for degraded (but that encourages retry). I prefer 200+warning/header.
ben: Implementation tradeoffs: many customers depend on status codes. If we use 200 for degraded, SDKs must inspect header/body to surface a special DegradedResponse exception if they want to surface it. That is a breaking change unless we version it.
carla: Runtime can emit header: `X-Redwood-Routing: degraded=v1;model=rw-small;fallback_reason=latency_shed` and a standardized body field `routing_hint` with enum values.
dmitri: For telemetry consistency we need a canonical enum: [normal, soft_degrade, hard_degrade, transient_error, terminal_error]. Map them to metrics and SLO buckets.
emily: Console copy: 'Soft degrade — served lower-capacity model to preserve latency. No customer action required. See logs.' and have a learn-more link. Keep accordions for examples.
alex: Rollout plan? We should do feature-flagged behavior: v1 header+body field + console badge -> opt-in SDK support -> 2-week telemetry sampling -> THEN firm contract.
rollout-bot: Canary rollout started for `routing-hint-header-v1` on 5% of traffic in us-west; flagged as `routing_hint_v1`.
laura: Also need clear quota messaging: differentiate tenant_quota_exhausted vs route_level_throttle. They look the same right now. Recommend distinct codes: `quota_exhausted` (do not retry), `route_throttle` (retry after backoff).
ben: Agree. Add HTTP hints: quota_exhausted = 429 with header Retry-After absent and body.reason=quota_exhausted. route_throttle = 429 with Retry-After and body.reason=route_throttle. That keeps 429 for rate cases, 2xx for served-but-degraded cases.
carla: Will update runtime PR to emit `X-Redwood-Routing` for degraded, `X-Redwood-ErrorKind` for failure kinds. Also will include numeric `routing_code` to help older SDKs.
dmitri: Create telemetry mapping doc snippet so SRE can map dashboards: `routing_code` -> prom label `redwood_route_outcome`. Add alerting rules for spikes in soft_degrade rate above 5% over baseline.
emily: UX ask: Console should surface actionable hint for quota_exhausted: link to upgrade/usage breakdown; for soft_degrade: link to model tunables and suggested caching.
alex: API docs + SDKs need test vectors. Please add unit tests and an integration test that asserts exact header/body patterns for: normal, soft_degrade, quota_exhausted, route_throttle, transient_error.
ben: I'll draft the RFC with these mappings. Suggest we include example SDK pseudocode for handling: ```js
const resp = await client.generate(...)
if (resp.headers['x-redwood-routing']?.includes('degraded')) {
  // surface as non-retryable DegradedResponse
}
if (resp.status === 429 && !resp.headers['retry-after']) {
  // treat as quota_exhausted -> do not retry
}
```
laura: Timeline: RFC this week, runtime PR next week, console flags next week -> canary + telemetry sampling week after. Ops/SRE signoff required before GA.
dmitri: I'll prepare dashboard queries and an initial alert proposal.
emily: I'll mock the console banners and copy for the RFC.
carla: I'll open a runtime PR and include examples of header payloads.
alex: Thanks — sounds like a plan. Small follow-ups: make sure we version the header `routing=v1` and include machine-friendly codes. Also document SDK migration path.
ben: Assigning action items in the RFC. @laura @carla @dmitri @emily please comment there. :thumbsup:
laura: :+1:
carla: will do
dmitri: ack
emily: adding drafts to the RFC document now
rollout-bot: Canary rollout `routing-hint-header-v1` updated: 10% -> 25% at 2024-03-12T15:12:00Z
